title: Prove three-query cubic repair solvability modulo every odd integer (no κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For every arity `r>=3` and every odd modulus `m>1`, the fixed cubic-reader defect is a sum of at most three weighted cubes modulo m, using primitive integer source rows. The explicit source-frame construction uses integer determinant-one shears and exact inverse words, restoring both arbitrary dirty sources exactly while reproducing the eager output modulo m. At most 31 source shears and three nonzero query slots suffice; neither is a modular minimum claim.

This closes one possible obstruction route in Nick Petalas's #6653 Open next question 1: **nonexistence in a finite odd quotient cannot prove an unrestricted four-query lower bound**. Any finite collection of congruences is covered by one witness for their least common multiple. The result does not settle exact global dyadic feasibility at r=15 or rule out valuation arguments constraining one fixed global representation.

The proof combines a three-cube identity integral at 3 with the rational extension of #6215's pure-B identity integral away from 3. CRT patches a common five-shear word, producing actual integer source frames rather than assuming matrix lifting. An exact-versus-modular counterexample makes the scope boundary executable.

**No new κ, physical cost saving or supplier admission.** The proof records every retained child, preparation/restoration frame and query; physical prices and remaining caller overhead are unknown. Modular output equality does not meet the original exact-output contract.

## Task, sources and overlap

Canonical upstream was pulled at entry and refreshed before publication, at `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. Task `joint-query-controller`, scope key `58d8c9133832c5149bdc`, explicitly **changed scope** to a bounded obstruction-method side result; the exact card and narrow family decision are in [TASK.json](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5da955b8abb379e939a3dd02821a62ead624f807/research/cubic-local-solubility/TASK.json).

Only `research/cubic-local-solubility/` is added. Three exact live sources are pinned at the base: #6653's node lemma/open question, #6215's identity/restricted modulo-nine obstruction, and #6212's general-frame contract. Neither #7475 (exact r24 repair) nor #7478 (fixed-weight Pell classification) is a dependency.

Fresh all-state PR body/title searches found no duplicate. The dedicated overlap helper could not obtain remote corpora because `gh` is absent, and cached Discussion pages do not establish complete current claim coverage. Those limits are recorded; no global novelty guarantee is claimed.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.14, macOS arm64, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/cubic-local-solubility
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/cubic-local-solubility --check-modes --check-source-history
python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py export --package research/cubic-local-solubility --ref HEAD --output /tmp/cubic-local.tar
python3.12 -B scripts/export_research_package.py check /tmp/cubic-local.tar
```

All four registered normal/optimized runs passed. Primary checks: two symbolic identities over Q[r], 3,682 literal integer-shear CRT certificates, seven algebra/program rejection controls, eight domain controls and three source-byte mutations. The independent checker imports neither primary nor predecessor code and instead uses primitive integer lifts and Bezout frames: rational expansions at r=3..128, 1,344 modular certificates, 5,376 dirty-input runs, three rejected faulty variants and a modulo-33 certificate that demonstrably fails exact output equality.

Committed bytes, executable modes and source history passed for all ten package/input files. Official export integrity passed. All four direct runs passed in a fresh read-only, Git-free export with empty PATH; all eleven files, including the receipt, retained their bytes and modes. The written proof establishes the infinite quantifiers; finite checks corroborate implementation. Separate Codex agents reviewed the proof and implementations; independent human/formal-kernel acceptance is not claimed.

Selected source-binding orientation passed; the selected scientific cold replay was not run because the selected construction is unchanged. Hosted CI is independently blocked at the base by `test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record`: selected frontier7000 versus stale frontier6030 navigation. The same sole failure appears in [#7475's planning job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43291062509/job/131437108801) and [#7478's planning job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43291772301/job/131439552156), before package replay. Existing #7276 covers that shared repair; this contribution does not duplicate it or weaken its test.

## Credit and next questions

Prepared by **apoursh** with substantial **OpenAI Codex and subagent assistance**. Credit Nick Petalas (#6200 reader/defect, #6653 node lemma and question), apoursh (#6212 contract, #6215 pure-B identity and restriction), and their retained predecessor lineage. Classical CRT, localization and elementary matrix methods are not claimed as new. Apache-2.0.

[Open next questions](https://github.com/apoursh/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5da955b8abb379e939a3dd02821a62ead624f807/research/cubic-local-solubility/README.md#open-next-questions): analyze global valuation compatibility across one exact rational triple at r=15, or specify a restricted direction contract that can still support a modular obstruction. The blockers are global dyadic integrality and precise restrictions preserved by reduction/patching, respectively.
